questions.text: Your colony is hosting a New Year party for all the families. What is your main contribution?

options.A: Organizing the lemon-and-spoon race, musical chairs, and tug-of-war for everyone to play.
options.B: Setting up the complex speaker system and explaining the rules of a new board game to the kids.
options.C: Taking over the mic, hosting the evening, and cracking jokes to keep the uncles and aunties entertained.
options.D: Managing the collection of money (chanda), creating a budget for snacks, and deciding the event schedule.

questions.text: Your Dada/Dadi (grandparents) just got a new smartphone. How do you help them?

options.A: Taking them out for a walk to the local market and practically showing them how to scan a QR code at the dairy shop.
options.B: Patiently showing them how to change font sizes, clear their RAM, and identifying spam links to keep them safe.
options.C: Making them practice sending voice notes and doing a mock WhatsApp video call from the next room so they get comfortable.
options.D: Sitting down to figure out exactly what apps they actually need, deleting the rest, and setting usage limits for them.

questions.text: The teacher leaves the class for 15 minutes, and chaos ensues. What are you doing?

options.A: Gathering your friends at the back benches to play a quick game of Dumb Charades or Pen Fight.
options.B: Putting up a tough Sudoku or Math puzzle on the blackboard to challenge the 'toppers' of the class.
options.C: Mimicking a strict teacher or telling a funny story to keep the whole class laughing and engaged.
options.D: Standing near the board like the Class Monitor, noting down who is making noise to maintain order.

questions.text: It's time for a massive SST (Social Studies) group project. What role do you take?

options.A: Forcing the group to meet at the nearest park or cafe so everyone can brainstorm actively without getting bored.
options.B: Doing the hardcore Google research, finding exact dates, and compiling all the factual data systematically.
options.C: Designing the chart paper, making the presentation look aesthetic, and deciding who will say what.
options.D: Assigning specific sections to each group member based on what they are good at, and ensuring they meet the deadline.

questions.text: Your school takes you on an educational trip to a historical fort. How are you spending the time?

options.A: Racing your friends up the steep stairs of the fort and organizing a game of hide-and-seek in the ruins.
options.B: Reading all the information plaques and explaining the architectural history and defense mechanisms to your friends.
options.C: Taking amazing photos for your friends, guiding their poses, and helping them write aesthetic Instagram captions.
options.D: Helping the teacher do headcounts and ensuring the group sticks to the timetable so you don't miss lunch.

questions.text: You have a free (substitution) period! How do you spend it with your squad?

options.A: Begging the PT sir to give you a basketball or cricket bat so you can play outside.
options.B: Helping a friend hack through a difficult Computer Science or Math assignment before the next period.
options.C: Rehearsing for the upcoming school Annual Day drama, dance, or debate competition.
options.D: Planning the exact schedule for your friend's upcoming birthday treat—who is paying what and which cafe to visit.

questions.text: Your best friend is terrified of giving a speech in the morning assembly. How do you fix it?

options.A: Making them jump around, shake out their arms, and do deep breathing exercises to kill the physical nerves.
options.B: Reviewing their script, fixing the grammar, and re-writing the points so they logically flow better.
options.C: Making them stand in front of you while you correct their voice modulation, eye contact, and hand gestures.
options.D: Reassuring them, and assessing if they are actually ready or if you should talk to the teacher about a backup speaker.

questions.text: You have just been made the Captain of your School House (Red/Blue/Green/Yellow). Your first move is:

options.A: Leading the march past practice with high energy and organizing intense tryouts on the sports field.
options.B: Creating a spreadsheet of all students in your house and analyzing past years' data to see who wins which medals.
options.C: Gathering your house in the auditorium and delivering an inspiring, cinematic speech to motivate them.
options.D: Strategically deciding which student participates in which event to maximize your house's overall points.

questions.text: When you and your friends play multiplayer games (like BGMI or Valorant), what is your style?

options.A: Hyping up the squad, yelling out enemy positions, and leading the aggressive charge into the fight.
options.B: Knowing exactly what each weapon's damage stats are, optimizing loadouts, and explaining the mechanics to the team.
options.C: Keeping the voice chat entertaining, trash-talking in fun, and narrating the clutch moments like a commentator.
options.D: Deciding the team strategy, allocating roles (who plays sniper, who plays medic), and making sure everyone does their job.

questions.text: What is honestly the best part about attending a big Indian wedding for you?

options.A: Being the first one on the dance floor and physically pulling your shy cousins and relatives to join the fun.
options.B: Fascinating over how the complex drone cameras, DJ consoles, or lighting setups actually work.
options.C: Choreographing the Sangeet performances and writing the funny script to roast the bride and groom.
options.D: Observing how the event managers coordinate the catering, time-keeping, and seating arrangements flawlessly.

Team_Building_Trainer.title: The Energy Booster (Outbound & Team-Building Trainer)
Team_Building_Trainer.primary_match_text: You have unmatched energy and love physical activity! You believe people learn best when they are moving, playing, and interacting. In the corporate world, you'd be the person taking stressed-out employees to resorts, making them play games to build trust and teamwork.
Team_Building_Trainer.day_in_the_life: Your day doesn't happen in an office. You are at a resort or outdoor camp, conducting trust-falls, treasure hunts, and leadership obstacle courses for managers of big MNCs. You break the ice and make adults feel like kids again.
Team_Building_Trainer.alternative_match_text: If not Corporate Training, you would make an amazing Sports Coach, Event Manager, or Adventure Tour Guide.
Team_Building_Trainer.roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th (Arts/Commerce preferred). Pursue a BBA or BA. Get specialized certifications in Experiential Learning, Outbound Training, or a degree in Physical Education (B.P.Ed) to master group dynamics.

Technical_Trainer.title: The Tech Guru (Technical Skills Trainer)
Technical_Trainer.primary_match_text: You are logical, detail-oriented, and love explaining complex systems! You don't just know how things work; you know how to teach others how things work. In the corporate world, you'd be the expert teaching employees how to code, use new software, or follow strict data rules.
Technical_Trainer.day_in_the_life: You are in a high-tech training room or on a massive Zoom call. You share your screen, explain complex software (like Excel, Python, or SAP), and help employees debug their errors patiently so they can do their jobs better.
Technical_Trainer.alternative_match_text: If not Corporate Training, you would thrive as a Software Engineer, IT Professor, or Tech Consultant.
Technical_Trainer.roadmap: Take PCM (Science) or Commerce with Math/Computer Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech, BCA, or B.Sc in IT/Computer Science. A Master's like MCA or specialized certifications (Microsoft, AWS, Cisco) will make you a highly paid tech trainer.

Soft_Skills_Coach.title: The Charmer (Soft Skills & Communication Coach)
Soft_Skills_Coach.primary_match_text: You have a way with words, expressions, and emotions! You understand that how you say something is as important as what you say. In the corporate world, you'd teach employees how to give powerful presentations, write polite emails, and handle angry clients.
Soft_Skills_Coach.day_in_the_life: You stand in front of a conference room filled with executives. You use beautiful PowerPoint slides, conduct role-play scenarios, and teach them body language, voice modulation, and empathy. You transform shy workers into confident leaders.
Soft_Skills_Coach.alternative_match_text: If not Corporate Training, you'd be a brilliant PR Manager, Motivational Speaker, or TV Anchor.
Soft_Skills_Coach.roadmap: Take Arts/Humanities or Commerce in 11th/12th. Pursue a BA in English, Psychology, or Mass Communication. Follow it up with an MBA in HR or certifications in NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming) and Corporate Etiquette.

HR_L_and_D_Head.title: The Mastermind (HR / L&D Head)
HR_L_and_D_Head.primary_match_text: You are a natural manager who sees the big picture! You don't just teach; you decide WHO needs to learn WHAT. In the corporate world, you would control the entire training budget and evaluate the performance of thousands of employees.
HR_L_and_D_Head.day_in_the_life: You sit in a corner office or the boardroom. You analyze performance reports, figure out why the sales team is failing, and then hire the right trainers to fix the problem. You track the training budget and ensure the company is constantly upgrading its talent.
HR_L_and_D_Head.alternative_match_text: If not Corporate Training, you would be a powerful HR Director, Business Operations Manager, or Management Consultant.
HR_L_and_D_Head.roadmap: Take Commerce or Arts in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA, B.Com, or BA in Psychology. The ultimate goal is to crack the CAT/XAT exams and get an MBA in Human Resources from a premier institute like XLRI Jamshedpur, TISS Mumbai, or an IIM.
